market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The 2028 election is an open-seat race with no incumbent running. Historical party win rates in such elections are broadly even (near 50%). Without candidate-specific information this far out, a 50% prior is more defensible. The current market price implies a 38.5% chance, significantly below the baseline, suggesting Yes shares are undervalued.
evidence_points: Open presidential elections (no incumbent) have historically been close to coin flips between the two major parties.
The absence of known candidates or economic conditions four years out makes extreme probabilities unjustified.
The 38.5% implied probability deviates from the long-run average of roughly 50% for either major party in any given election.
